evals.name: library-from-specs
evals.prompt: We have the L1/L2 requirements for Shelf (library lending: catalog, members, loans, returns, holds) in docs/specs. Build the HTML mocks for the whole product so the team can click through it before we start the Angular work.
evals.expected_output: docs/mocks/ with manifest.json, README.md (cast, coverage matrix, open questions), index.html gallery, shared assets, and one HTML file per page/dialog/notification per state; requirement IDs copied verbatim from docs/specs into the manifest and mock:requirements metas; check_mocks.py exits 0.
expectations: docs/mocks/manifest.json lists pages, dialogs and notifications, including sign-in, password reset, 404, 403, error and offline pages that the specs do not mention explicitly

Every page listed in the manifest has default, loading, empty and error state files (or a not_applicable reason), every dialog has default, busy and invalid, and every notification has info, success, warning and danger
Every mock links docs/mocks/assets/tokens.css and ui.css; no raw hex/rgb/hsl colours appear in page styles or style attributes
Every mock has doctype, lang, title, viewport, one h1, a main landmark, mock:kind/mock:screen/mock:state metas matching its path, and a .mock-bar linking its sibling states
Requirement IDs in the manifest and mock:requirements metas match identifiers that exist verbatim in docs/specs
No mock contains lorem ipsum, TODO, TBD or generic names like John Doe; the same cast of people and items recurs across mocks
Dialog mocks render the dialog over its originating page with role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby and an inert page behind
Notification mocks place toasts in a role=status live region on the page that triggers them and include an undo action for reversible operations
Running check_mocks.py --write exits 0 and README.md contains the generated coverage matrix with no ❌ cells
Screenshots at 360, 768 and 1280 px in light and dark were produced (or the missing browser was reported) and no screenshot shows horizontal overflow or clipped text

evals.name: add-missing-states
evals.prompt: The mocks in docs/mocks only have the happy path. Add the loading, empty, error and validation states everywhere they are missing and make sure dark mode works.
evals.expected_output: Existing mocks preserved; new state files derived from each default with identical layout; manifest and coverage updated; dark theme verified via tokens; checker exits 0.
expectations: Existing default.html files are not rewritten beyond adding mock:* metas and the mock bar if they were missing
Each page gains loading.html using layout-matching skeletons, empty.html with an explanation and one call to action, and error.html that keeps the page chrome and offers a retry
Each page with a form gains invalid.html with inline field errors, aria-invalid, aria-describedby and an error summary
The manifest lists every new state and the coverage matrix in README.md is regenerated with the new columns filled
Any raw colour found in the existing mocks is replaced with a token so the dark theme applies everywhere
check_mocks.py exits 0 with no orphan files

evals.name: no-specs-from-description
evals.prompt: Mock up a small invoicing app: list invoices, create/edit an invoice, send it, mark it paid, and a settings page for company details. Nothing is written down yet.
evals.expected_output: A complete mock set derived from the description with assumptions recorded; no requirement IDs invented.
expectations: docs/mocks/README.md records the assumptions made in the absence of docs/specs under an Open questions section
No mock:requirements meta or manifest requirements array contains invented identifiers
The set includes pages for invoices list, invoice detail, new/edit invoice, settings, sign in, 404 and error, dialogs for send and mark-as-paid, and toasts for sent/paid/failed
The invoice list has default, loading, empty, error and no-results states; the invoice form has default, invalid, submitting and success states
Monetary values use consistent formatting with thousands separators and currency, and dates are human-readable
check_mocks.py exits 0

evals.name: consume-existing-design-system
evals.prompt: docs/design-system already exists. Add mocks for the new 'holds' feature (list holds, place a hold dialog, hold-ready notification) using the system, not new styles.
evals.expected_output: New mocks link ../../design-system/tokens/tokens.css and assets/components.css, use its classes, and add nothing to docs/mocks/assets beyond mock.css/mock.js.
expectations: New mock files link the design system's tokens.css and components.css rather than a local ui.css copy
No new component CSS is written inside the mocks; a genuinely new component is added to docs/design-system with its own page instead
The manifest gains the holds page, place-hold dialog and hold-ready notification with all required states
check_mocks.py exits 0 and the gallery shows the new screens
